units.translation: 983. φηλώσῃς: you may deceive; from φήληξ, the unripe fig.
993. To Hellas having returned: Hellas here means the whole Phthiotic land, homonymously with the city, just as Argos is both the city and the land.

997-1004a. δή ποτέ καὶ Θησῆα: through these words he ethically invites Medea to sail away with him, bringing forward the example of Ariadne, that she departed with Theseus to Athens and because of Ariadne's love; that Athens in L2(P) : omitted in L1, where a lacuna is indicated by K, supplemented by W
23 the beginning of the scholium up to Ἀθήνας is repeated in L at the end, cf. W Phil. 81, 1926, 20

25 τὴν Ἀριάδνην in L1 : τὸν Ariadnes erota in L2P

For Theseus' safety her crown was placed among the stars. Neither of these is true. For she was left behind by Theseus on Naxos; and she was deflowered by Dionysus according to some, from whom she bears Oenopion, Thoas, Staphylus, Latramys, Euanthes, Tauropolis. That Minos did not consent to the marriage of Ariadne nor did Theseus bring her to Athens, Homer says expressly, and that she died abandoned by Theseus, through what Odysseus says (λ 321. 22. 24): 'Phaedra and Procris I saw, and fair Ariadne, daughter of Minos of baneful mind, whom once Theseus married but had no joy of her.' That the crown was placed among the stars by Dionysus, Aratus says (Phaen. 71 sq.): 'there too is that crown, which glorious Dionysus set as a sign of departed Ariadne.'

1013-14a. προπρὸ δ’ ἀφειδήσασα: it is written προπρὸ δὲ μειδήσασα. The repetition of the preposition is erotic; for it indicates more that the giving happened with eagerness and readily.
b. ἀφειδήσασα: having been careless of addressing. Instead of: no longer being precise or meddling, she took the drug from her breast-band. Through this the intensity of her love is shown.
